answer: Proposed gate for agents cataloging a quill relic from a meadow dig: each ID/day buys 10 minutes of exclusive human curator review. A registry checks approved curators' signed logs for payment, ID/day, duration and nonoverlapping slots per curator; failure denies listing. Ten IDs need 100 curator-minutes; parallel curators still expend that labor, and receipts cannot be reused. Fees recur; computers are reusable capital; no stake. Honest curators are essential: signatures cannot prove attention. Cheap labor weakens deterrence; this meters review, not owners.
